big: Dadi wants to lend money to someone who will certainly pay her back. The safest borrower in India is the government itself. She can buy its bonds, and since 2021 she can do it directly through RBI's retail platform.

lines: Very low risk of default, since the government repays from its own taxes and borrowing. But their prices can still move when interest rates change, so they are not without risk.

rows: A bond from the central government, with very low credit risk
A short-term security, sold at a discount and repaid at face value
A bond from a state government, sold at an auction
A platform where individuals buy government securities directly
note: Treasury bills are issued for 91, 182 and 364 days.
The gain comes from the gap between the price paid and the face value.

q: Meena buys a treasury bill at ₹97.50 with a face value of ₹100. What happens at maturity?
why: A bill is repaid at face value, so she gains the gap.
That is what she paid, so there would be no gain.
A bill pays no coupon. Its gain is the discount.
The central government repays at maturity, so nothing is wrong.

q: Why is a central government security seen as having very low credit risk?
opts: The price never changes at any time
It pays the highest return of all bonds
It can raise money to repay its own debt
It is run by a bank, not the state
why: Prices of government securities do move when interest rates change.
Low risk usually goes with lower returns, not the highest.
The government repays in its own currency from taxes and borrowing.
It is issued by the government, not by a bank.

q: Rohan wants to buy government securities directly, without a middleman fund. What can he use?
why: A shop counter does not sell government securities.
It is a platform where individuals buy government securities directly.
A chit fund is a different arrangement and not a government security.
A social media group is not a safe way to buy securities.

q: A state government borrows by issuing bonds through an auction. What is this bond called?
opts: A treasury bill of the centre
A fixed deposit in a bank
why: A treasury bill is a short-term central security.
An NCD is a bond issued by a company, not a state.
A fixed deposit is placed with a bank and is not a state bond.
States raise funds by selling these loans at auctions.

pts: A G-Sec is a government bond with very low credit risk.
A treasury bill is sold at a discount and repaid at face value.
RBI Retail Direct lets individuals buy government securities directly.
